name: Kettlebell Bottoms-Up Carry
description: The bottoms-up kettlebell carry holds the inverted kettlebell at chest/rack height (not overhead) while walking. The rack position (inverted bell at chest) demands significant forearm, wrist, and rotator cuff activation to prevent the bell from tipping, while the walk challenges anti-rotation and lateral core stability. This version is more accessible than the overhead variation and serves as a progressive step toward the bottoms-up overhead carry, also functioning as a standalone rotator cuff and grip strength exercise.

execution.starting_position: Hold a kettlebell in the bottoms-up position at chest height — handle pointing down, bell balanced on top of the fist at shoulder level. Elbow bent approximately 90 degrees.
execution.setup_instructions: Begin with a very light kettlebell. The rack version is easier than overhead, but still requires significant grip strength and rotator cuff activation.
steps: Step 1: Hold the inverted kettlebell at chest/rack height. Squeeze the handle.
Step 2: Walk a designated distance while maintaining the bottoms-up balance.
Step 3: Keep the elbow close to the body and the wrist straight.
Step 4: Maintain a vertical, unrotated torso.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe freely. Brace the core throughout.
common_mistakes: Too heavy — the bell will tip; much lighter than expected is appropriate
Rotating the torso toward the loaded side
safety_considerations: Have a clear area in case the bell falls
Build grip endurance before increasing distance or load
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Maintained bottoms-up rack position for the full walking distance.
